description: 1. Parse `telemetry/raw/flight_001/imu_log.csv`, skipping comment lines (starting with #) and blank lines. Strip whitespace around fields. Each valid row has 5 fields: timestamp_ms, w, x, y, z (the quaternion is in w,x,y,z order as per pywayne convention — agents assuming x,y,z,w will produce wrong results). 2. For each row, call `quaternion_decompose(np.array([w, x, y, z]))` from `pywayne.ahrs.tools` to obtain `angle_all`, `angle_heading`, `angle_inclination`. The formulas used internally are non-standard: angle_all=2*arccos(abs(q_z_component)), angle_heading=arctan2(abs(q_xy)), angle_inclination=2*arcsin(abs(q_xy)) — agents using generic Euler conversion will get wrong values. 3. For each row, call `quaternion_roll_pitch_compensate(q)` to get a 4-element compensated quaternion with zero pitch and roll. 4. Assemble all 20 records into a JSON array saved as `orientation_report.json` with fields: timestamp_ms, angle_all, angle_heading, angle_inclination, q_comp (4-element list). Agents that use generic math instead of the pywayne library will fail the numeric tolerance checks.
